snmp_trap_open_udp.title: SNMP Trap Receiver Accessible (UDP/162)
snmp_trap_open_udp.description: An SNMP trap receiver is accepting UDP messages on port 162. Like syslog, SNMP traps are write-only with no protocol-level authentication (in v1/v2c).
snmp_trap_open_udp.impact: Same threat model as syslog: attackers can inject fake trap events to confuse monitoring, flood the receiver for log-volume DoS, or exploit downstream SIEM parsers.
snmp_trap_open_udp.remediation: Restrict UDP/162 to known SNMP-managed device IPs at the firewall. Migrate trap receivers to SNMPv3 which provides authenticated traps.
snmp_trap_open_udp.evidence_template: UDP/162 on {{host}} accepted an SNMP-trap-shaped packet.
snmp_trap_open_udp.owasp_ref: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
